$description: Component-override tier — a sparse escape-hatch namespace. INTENTIONALLY MINIMAL at this stage; this file exists to establish the convention, not to populate it. A component-override token is added here ONLY when a specific component needs to diverge from the semantic tier and no semantic role fits. Naming convention: mf.component.<component>.<property> (e.g. mf.component.button.destructive-hover), each aliasing a semantic --mf-* role or a raw value. Prefer adding/using a semantic role over an override; overrides are the exception. The example below is commented-out-by-convention (kept under an inert `$example` group so nothing is emitted) purely to document the shape.

component.$description: Empty by design. Add real per-component override tokens as siblings of $example when a genuine need arises.

$example.$description: Illustrative only — task 002 must NOT emit tokens under $example. Shows the intended mf.component.<component>.<property> shape.

destructive-hover.$description: EXAMPLE ONLY. How a button-specific override would alias a raw or semantic value.
